title: Nature Boost - Protocol for a feasibility study on VR-based nature interventions for residents and nurses in long-term care facilities.
summary:
The Nature Boost (MNB) feasibility study explores the effectiveness of implementing virtual nature experiences using virtual reality (VR) headsets in long-term care facilities. The study aims to assess the acceptance of this technology by residents and nursing staff, its potential positive impact on factors such as sleep, stress, well-being and trust in caregiving relationships, and the further opportunities and challenges associated with the intervention.
Access to natural environments is often restricted for people with limited mobility. VR technology enables them to virtually immerse themselves in a forest setting. In this study, ten residents will watch a 360° forest video several times per week for four weeks, usually before bedtime. Nursing staff will support them either by assisting with the technical setup or by participating in the nature experience together with the residents.
The study will investigate how practical the use of this technology is, and how the intervention is perceived by participants. The study will also explore whether the intervention has beneficial effects on sleep, mood, well-being and feelings of loneliness among residents, as well as on perceived stress among nursing staff. Changes in mutual trust between residents and caregivers will also be considered.
The results will inform the design of a larger follow-up study which will evaluate an enhanced multisensory nature experience incorporating additional natural stimuli, such as sounds and smells.
conditions: The focus of the MNB feasibility study is: (a) the feasibility of VR-based nature interventions for health promotion and prevention in long-term care facilities, including potential barriers and facilitators to implementation; (b) sleep quality, well-being, loneliness and depressive symptoms among residents; (c) perceived stress and burnout risk among nursing staff.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
A total of 20 participants (10 residents and 10 nurses) will be recruited from two long-term care facilities. Sampling will follow a maximum variation strategy to ensure diversity of perspective. Recruitment will be conducted by facility management and staff representatives.
Exclusion criteria:
Individuals with health conditions that are incompatible with VR use are excluded. These include psychotic disorders; the presence of medical devices that are sensitive to magnetic fields, such as pacemakers or VP shunts; physical or psychological impairments that prevent the ability to give informed consent; and contraindications to the use of VR headsets, such as epilepsy or severe balance disorders.
